podcast.title: "Silly Love Songs" Accusation
podcast.body: As they prepared to record Paul McCartney's fifth album following The Beatles' breakup, Paul McCartney's new band, Wings, was accused by critics of producing "nothing more than silly love songs." This criticism contributed to the perception that McCartney was struggling to redefine his artistic direction post-Beatles. "His new band Wings was accused of creating nothing more than silly love songs as they were getting ready to record McCartney's fifth album since the breakup of his other band."

podcast.title: Album Art Designed by Storm Thorgerson
podcast.body: Wings' album covers were among the many iconic designs created by the renowned Storm Thorgerson and his partner Aubrey Powell. Their joint efforts contributed to the visual representation of this post-Beatles project. "That includes Pink Floyd, Black Sabbath, Led Zeppelin, ACDC, the police, Genesis, Peter Gabriel, ELO, Paul McCartney, and Wings..."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Stories Behind Iconic Album Covers Part 2

podcast.title: Pre-Nigeria Lineup Changes
podcast.body: Before the band even departed for EMI studios in Nigeria to record the *Band on the Run* album, two members of Wings quit, adding to the difficult and chaotic circumstances surrounding the album's production. "It started with two band members quitting wings before they even left for Nigeria".

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Ambition to Surpass Inspiral Carpets
xref.body: Keyboardist Clint Boon of the Inspiral Carpets observed that Noel Gallagher "was always writing songs" and "had a swagger," suggesting his potential. Noel himself, watching from the wings, thought, "I can do better than this," indicating his strong ambition to transcend his roadie role and outperform the band he was working for. "Watching them from the wings, he said, I thought, I can do better than this."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: We Are The Road Crew - A History of Roadies

xref.title: Comic Book Artist and Creator
xref.body: Gerard Way began his journey in comic books at the age of 16, with his first comic, "On Raven's Wings," having two issues published. By 2001, he was interning as a sketch artist at Cartoon Network in New York, where he pitched an animated TV series called "The Breakfast Monkey," though it was not picked up. The experience of living through 9/11 profoundly impacted him, prompting him to leave animation to pursue music, which led to the formation of My Chemical Romance. In 2007, he began work on the mini-series "The Umbrella Academy," which became a significant success and was later adapted into a popular Netflix series. He also worked with the Marvel Universe on Spider-Man, creating the character of Penny Parker. "It was Gerard Way that created the character of Penny Parker."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Career and Persona
xref.body: Susan Dietrich, known as The Space Lady, is from Pueblo, Colorado. For many years, she was a street musician, frequently performing in cities like Boston and San Francisco. She was easily recognizable by her unique outfit: a silver plastic helmet adorned with white wings and a flashing light. She initially played the accordion. "She wore a silver plastic helmet adorned with white wings and a flashing light on top. And she played the accordion."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Historical Background
xref.body: Located in rural France, this was a French château built in 1740 on the remnants of a 16th-century structure. It featured two wings, 30 rooms, a swimming pool, a tennis court, outbuildings, and 42,000 acres of parkland. "It was an honest-to-god French château that was built in 1740 on the remains of an earlier building that dated back to sometime in the mid-16th century."

xref.title: Medical Support for Final Tour
xref.body: For the "Man-Machine Poem" tour, a dedicated EMS team was hired specifically for Gord Downie, and his surgeon, Dr. Douglas DJ Cook, was present backstage as a precaution due to concerns about seizures from dehydration and sleep deprivation. "A separate EMS team was hired just for Gord to go on tour. Dr. Cook, Gord's surgeon, was in the wings."

xref.body: The band was instrumental in carrying Goth music beyond its UK birthplace by the mid-1980s, alongside Siouxsie and the Banshees and The Cure. "It was carried on the wings of music, sisters of mercy, suzzy in the banshees and the cure."

xref.title: The Log Guitar Design
xref.body: "The log" was a rudimentary solid-body electric guitar constructed from a 4x4 piece of pine, to which two wings were attached to mimic the appearance of a Spanish guitar. It featured a regular guitar neck, a bridge, and two crude homemade pickups, making it distinct from the hollow-body electric guitars available at the time. "The result was something he called the log. It was a 4x4 piece of pine with two wings attached to it to make it look like a Spanish guitar. He attached a regular guitar neck to that body, along with a bridge and two crude homemade pickups. Unlike all the other electric guitars in the market, this one wasn't hollow. Its body was solid."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Story of the Electric Guitar - Part 1

xref.title: U2's Mentorship on Tour
xref.body: While on tour with U2, Kings of Leon received invaluable guidance on the intricacies of the "business side of touring," including lessons on lighting and creating a distinctive stage show. Jared Followill noted U2's meticulous attention to detail, such as washing lights before every performance. This contrasted sharply with Kings of Leon's own practice of often foregoing soundchecks, with their first chord of a show often being their initial chord of the evening. "They kind of took us under their wings for that whole tour and taught us a lot of stuff that we still use to this day. On the business side of touring stuff. As far as lighting and just having a really big, unique show."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Kings of Leon in Their Own Words: Part 1
